summary: Flame in Freefall: Microgravity Combustion Insights is an interactive Super Intelligence (SI) powered fire safety dashboard built with real experimental data from the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository. Since fire behaves unpredictably in reduced gravity because of how the absence of buoyancy-driven airflow changes how flames spread and consume oxygen, we wanted to turn complex experimental data into an navigable tool that helps engineers and safety planners predict and prevent fire hazards before they happen. Our application uses 35 experimental records across NASA’s SAFFIRE-2, BASS, and FLEX missions and turns them into a risk assessment tool for both spacecraft habitats and low-ventilation Earth structures. Users can test mission presets including the ISS, Artemis Lunar Habitats, and Earth subway tunnels or customize oxygen concentration, cabin pressure, and ventilation airflow. Based on extensive research from the PSI repository, we ordered a scoring engine that ranks material flammability in real time. Additionally, we integrated an SI Mission Safety Briefing module that generates a tailored suppression and safety mitigation procedure to protect astronauts and other infrastructure alike.
details:
What Does It Do & How Does It Work?
It's an interactive fire-safety simulation dashboard built on 35 experimental records from NASA’s PSI repository spanning the SAFFIRE-2, BASS, and FLEX microgravity combustion experiments.
Users can load mission presets (such as the ISS Standard Cabin, Artemis Lunar Habitat, or an Earth Subway/Tunnel), or adjust Oxygen Concentration (12%–40%), Cabin Pressure (50–310 kPa), and Ventilation Airflow (0–30 cm/s) via interactive sliders. In real time, a physics-ordered risk engine weights these variables (40% Oxygen Concentration, 30% Baseline Material Burn/Spread Rate, 20% Ventilation Airflow, and 10% Cabin Pressure) to calculate a 1–100 risk score and sort the materials into Safe, Caution, or Critical levels. Users can also select any NASA experiment and use the SI Mission Safety Briefing feature to ask custom questions and generate tailored fire-suppression procedures.
Benefits & Intended Impact
  • Safer space exploration, as we prepare for long Moon and Mars missions that operate at higher oxygen levels and lower pressures than the ISS, mission planners need quick and efficient ways to evaluate cabin material flammability under forced HVAC airflow
  • Fire Prevention, because microgravity isolates combustion without buoyancy-driven conditions, NASA’s data reflects tight, low-ventilation fires on Earth such as inside subway tunnels, aircraft cargo holds, HVAC ducts, and building wall cavities so our tool bridges space research and engineering to improve fire suppression readiness
Tools, Languages & Software Used
  • Python, Streamlit (web dashboard and UI), and Pandas (data cleaning, normalization, and risk scoring)
  • Data Sources: NASA Physical Sciences Informatics Open Data Repository (SAFFIRE-2, BASS, and FLEX test datasets)
  • Super Intelligence we used was Google Gemini (assisted with UI structuring & code formatting), GitHub, and Streamlit Community Cloud for deployment
Creativity & Key Factors Considered
  • We creatively mapped NASA’s zero-buoyancy datasets to Earth’s most dangerous enclosed environments, applying distinct safety-margin scaling factors depending on the selected input
  • Our team carefully weighed the primary drivers of microgravity combustion, prioritizing oxygen concentration and material burn/spread rates alongside forced ventilation airflow which acts as the primary oxygen delivery mechanism without natural airflow
